newsitem.title: USA: US March stock funds net cash flow $10.51 bln -- ICI.
newsitem.headline: US March stock funds net cash flow $10.51 bln -- ICI.

text.p: Net new cash flow into U.S. stock mutual funds was $10.51 billion in March, compared with $18.16 billion in February, the Investment Company Institute said on Tuesday.
ICI said flows to stock funds in the first three months of 1997 totaled $57.75 billion, compared with $72.54 billion for the same period in 1996.
ICI said bond and income funds had an outflow of $1.99 billion in March, compared with an inflow of $2.26 billion in February.
Inflows to bond and income funds totalled $3.87 billion in the first quarter, compared with $7.98 billion in the first quarter of 1996, ICI said.
Money market funds had an inflow of $872.4 million in March, compared with inflows of $21.12 billion in February.
Among stock fund inflows, domestic equity funds accounted for $44.37 billion, or 76.8 percent of the total, the same proportion as in the first quarter of 1996.
March's reduced inflow combined with declines of major domestic stock indexes to reduce the value of total stock fund assets to $1.810 trillion.

ICI said combined total assets of the nation's mutual funds were $3.663 trillion in March, compared with $3.731 trillion in February and $3.036 trillion in March 1996. Total assets include taxable and non-taxable money market funds.
ICI said the outflow in bond funds, after four consecutive months of net inflows, was due in large part to an outflow of $1.25 billion in the high-yield category.
